title: Assurance Murmur: SOC2 prep notes
content:
(personal scratchpad) — rapid brain dump for evidence threads, control mapping, what to ask auditors, and small scripts to gather proof. Not polished. Use as working ledger.

Top-level goals:
- Quick inventory of low-friction evidence we can produce this week.
- Identify 3 small docs to finalize for readiness: access-review proof, change-control snapshot, backup/restoration validation.
- Draft canned answers for auditor Qs re: key management, incident response, and deployment isolation.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Do we have a single canonical runbook for emergency key rotations? I think only half of SREs have the doc. Confluence link above is a draft.
- Need clarity on which Dedicated instances are still on older AMIs (affects patch-control evidence). Ask infra to produce AMI inventory (JIRA-1348).
- How long do we actually store shard logs in object storage before lifecycle moves to glacier? Policy says 90 days but I suspect some buckets are grandfathered. Need list.

Quick evidence candidates (fast wins):
1) IAM access-review export: run weekly query -> produce CSV with user, role, last-used timestamp (script in repo PR/556).
2) KMS key metadata snapshot: key policy, creation date, rotation flag -> fine for sample of 3 customer KMS keys (hosted, dedicated, private).
3) Job: backups-success-30d report from backup-service -> provide hash/snapshot for 3 sample days.
4) Change control demo: pick 1 small infra PR with proper peer review + CI run + deployment log -> shows pipeline + approval gating.

Mapping notes (rough) — local mapping shorthand to SOC2 common criteria. Keep these short, we will formalize later.
- CC6.1 / Logical access: IAM review + MFA enforcement + SSO SAML settings export.
- CC6.2 / Least privilege: role definitions + example role-binding YAMLs + RBAC audits.
- CC7.1 / Configuration change management: PR history + CI trace + deployment timestamps.
- CC8.3 / Backup & recovery: backup logs + restore test result note.
- CC9.2 / Incident response: incident timeline + postmortem + comms template.

Evidence collection heuristics (how I plan to get each):
- For IAM: use `aws iam generate-credential-report` for account-level snapshot, combine with CloudTrail LookupEvents filtered by ConsoleLogin and AssumeRole. Save as evidence.csv with accompanying query used.
- For KMS: `aws kms list-keys` -> describe-key -> capture KeyPolicy and RotationStatus; store as kms-KEYID-policy.json.
- For backups: query backup-service API: `/api/v1/backups/status?site=prod&days=30` -> archive output with SHA256 and manifest.

Mini-scripts (notes to self)
- IAM last-used export (one-liner idea):
  aws iam get-account-authorization-details --filter User,Role | jq '.UserDetailList[] | {UserName,PasswordLastUsed,AccessKeyLastUsed}' > iam-snapshot.json

- KMS snapshot:
  for id in $(aws kms list-keys --query 'Keys[].KeyId' -r); do aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id $id; aws kms get-key-policy --key-id $id --policy-name default > key-$id-policy.json; done

- Backup-call: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_TOKEN" "https://backup.internal/api/status?days=30" > backups-30d.json

Draft canned answers (short):
Q: How are keys rotated and who can rotate them?
A: Rotation is enabled for customer-facing KMS keys by default. Rotation operations are restricted to the KeyOps group (IAM role: arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/KeyOps) and require MFA and a peer approval step in the Key Ops runbook. We will attach the runbook and an execution log for the sample rotation in Jan-2026. (Need to find final runbook link).

Q: How do you ensure only authorized code is deployed to production?
A: Deploys pass through CI with required status checks (unit/integration), a mandatory code review from at least one engineer with write access, and a signed release tag. Autonomous deploys are blocked unless flagged by Release Engineering. Provide PR #556 and associated pipeline run as control evidence.

Q: What is your incident escalation path?
A: Incident starts with alerting -> triage channel (#oncall-ecs) -> severity classification -> incident manager assigned -> contain/mitigate steps executed -> retrospective + postmortem published. Attach a redacted postmortem (incident-2026-01-14) showing timeline and action items.

Items to finalize (this sprint):
- [ ] Pull IAM credential report and sanitize PII -> place in evidence bucket (deadline: 2026-03-12).
- [ ] Confirm AMI inventory & note any non-compliant hosts (ask infra team, JIRA-1348).
- [ ] Export KMS policies for three sample keys and secure them to evidence/keys/.
- [ ] Run one restore test and capture console output + timestamp.
- [ ] Draft short narrative for auditor attaching the above artifacts (1 page).

Things to call out to infra / SRE slack: (send short messages)
- @infra: need AMI inventory CSV by EOD Tues (context: SOC2 prep). Link JIRA.
- @sre: can we run a scheduled restore test on 2026-03-11? I'll coordinate pre-window.
- @security: who owns the final key rotation runbook? (cc: Samira)

Risks / gotchas (personal notes):
- Some evidence will reveal ticket numbers and engineer usernames; plan to redact or replace with role names for auditor delivery. Keep originals in a sealed evidence storage path (auditor-only).
- We may not have a single consolidated log-retention policy doc that explicitly calls out the 90-day number across all subsystems. Need to clarify policy vs practice.

Last-minute checklist for handoff to auditor:
- Create an evidence manifest (CSV) describing artifact name, type, date range, redaction status, and access path.
- Ensure each artifact has a reproducible command used to generate it (so auditors can trust the snapshot).
- For any demo, script the steps so the demo is repeatable in case auditor asks to re-run.

Notes to self:
- Keep this file as the working ledger until 2026-03-15, then move finalized notes -> confluence/trust-ops/soc2-readiness.
- Save incremental snapshots as `assurance-murmur-v1.json` etc in folder so I can revert.

Random thoughts / fragments:
- Could sample a dedicated tenant with only infra logs to show isolation story.
- Maybe create a one-page 'how we serve requests' diagram focused purely on access boundaries; simple box diagram + short narrative.
- If audit asks for encryption at rest proof beyond KMS metadata, find a disk encryption policy or storage class setting.

End of scratchpad.

(If you are reading later: this is intentionally messy — follow the TODOs above and convert to proper artifacts. Ping Evan/Samira for quick pairing on KMS snapshot.)
